samples_reviewed.question_text: Use base-10 blocks to show the number 35.
Use base-10 blocks to show the number 68.
What number is marked on the number line?
Move the dot to show 85 on the number line.
What number do the blocks show?
Move the dot to show 99 on the number line.
Move the dot to show 77 on the number line.
What number is marked on the number line?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Representation is asked in both directions the competency implies - building a quantity with a model, as in the instruction to use base-10 blocks to show the number 35, and recognising a quantity from a model already shown on a number line or in blocks.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The stated variety of models is only partly realised: base-10 blocks and the number line carry all eight samples, with no bar model and no other concrete grouping, and the values used never drop below the mid-thirties, so the ten-and-ones structure of small two-digit numbers is never modelled.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Placing a dot on a number line and assembling tens and ones are the standard concrete-to-pictorial bridges for Quarter 1 of Grade 1, and each stem is a single imperative or a single question with no multi-step reasoning.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Two model families each appear in both a construct form and a read form - move the dot to show 99 on the number line against asking what number is marked on it - which gives the pupil four genuinely different encounters rather than one repeated frame.

competency_alignment.rationale: The block-reading item pits 83 against 38 and a plausible small value, which tests place value in the model itself, and the number-line items sit the target next to its immediate neighbours; both keep the difficulty on representation rather than on arithmetic.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values run up to 99 with 100 present as an option on the number line item, so the stated ceiling is reached without being exceeded, and the quantities remain modellable in tens and ones.
